name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to third-party dependencies.

This keeps our codebase clean without manual review overhead. The trade-off is trusting the formatter’s safety, but formatting-only changes can’t break logic.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "formatting-only" — it’s that formatting tools often embed hidden logic tweaks (e.g., line-wrap rules that alter string literals or comments). A safer alternative is to auto-apply *only* whitespace changes via a dedicated linter like Prettier with `--check` mode, then gatekeep logic edits manually. Settle it by running a diff audit: if any change touches non-whitespace, reject the patch.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Prettier’s `--write` mode, but only after running `--check` in CI to block any non-whitespace changes. This keeps the codebase clean without manual review while proving the formatter hasn’t altered logic. The trade-off is accepting Prettier’s opinionated style as the standard, which may conflict with some team preferences but ensures consistency.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "whitespace-only"—it’s that third-party dependencies often include minified or obfuscated code where even a single character shift can break functionality. A safer alternative is to auto-apply *only* to your own codebase with a pre-commit hook, not third-party dependencies. Settle it by proving the formatter’s `--check` mode catches all non-whitespace changes in a full CI run.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches *only* to our own generated code and third-party dependencies *after* Prettier `--check` passes in CI, but skip third-party minified/obfuscated files.

Result: Clean codebase with zero manual review for safe formatting, no logic risks. Owner: Sprocket.
